_comment: Three-band ledger for physical-properties/index.mjs, the paint half of the one-direction law. `pinnedDebt` and `inert` pin a COUNT PER FILE, not a line list: an edit above a site would move every number without changing anything the law cares about. `pinnedDebt` is a physical edge that should be logical -- growth fails, a fix fails with an instruction to lower the pin. `inert` is a symmetric pair or a centred offset, where flipping the direction moves nothing: it is COUNTED rather than excluded by rule, because proving symmetry pair-by-pair is fragile and a pinned band is what stops tomorrow's unpaired `left: 0` arriving unnoticed; clearing one is a zero-pixel change. `namedExceptions` are declared PER SITE, as a locator (`scope property: value`, whitespace-collapsed) with its own reason: each exempts exactly the one site it names, so a second physical site in the same file is judged as unbanded and a substituted site stops matching its locator -- the exception is never permission for the whole file. Frozen engines (223 of the 245 measured sites) are excluded by path in the gate source, because the freeze gate already governs them with written, content-pinned exceptions. Population measured 2026-09-16; the Class D corrections lot then cleared the two LIVE debt rows -- the countdown affix gap to marginInlineEnd/marginInlineStart on --ds-spacing-1 and the progress label to textAlign:'end'. The same day the detector moved from a spelling regex to the TypeScript syntax tree, which found eight sites the regex could not see (keys inside spreads, branches of a conditional style and CSSProperties-returning functions); each is banded below and says so in its reason. There are TWO exception classes. The first is MEASURED SPACE: a value that arrives from `getBoundingClientRect()` or a pointer event is already a physical viewport coordinate, so a logical inset would mirror an already-mirrored number. The second, opened by the INV-01 adjudication, is PHYSICAL PLACEMENT VOCABULARY: a site whose paired placement API or CSS keywords are physical by contract (`placement: 'left' | 'right'`, `position-area: left | span-right`), where a logical spelling would move the paint OFF the side the caller asked for under RTL; migrating such a site means migrating its vocabulary first, which is a separate work order. The INV-01 lot then cleared four of the five debt rows: the slider migrated FIVE of its six vertical anchors to `insetInlineStart` -- the step dot, the range track, both handles and the vertical mark label -- and gained the `:dir(rtl)` rail/track/dot skin mirrors they needed, keeping the value tooltip pinned as debt owed to the placement-vocabulary lot of WO-INV-01; the mark label is the site the retired slider pin called the DEFECT (`left: '100%'` in `renderMarks`, which under RTL put the label on the far side of the root, away from the rail) and it is the one that was fixed, pinned by `primitives/inputs/slider/tests/Slider.mark-label-direction.test.tsx`; the dropdown DROPPED the caller's physical `left` forward (measured consumers of `overlayStyle.left` on an in-tree placement: 0 across core, showroom, bithire, evnto and platform); affix was granted a named exception in the measured-space class (precedent export-button/filter-dropdown/chart-tooltip), and overlay positioning `offsetMargins` stays pinned as debt owed to the same placement-vocabulary lot of WO-INV-01 (DT ruling 2026-09-16: a physical placement vocabulary is this work order's scope, so it cannot be exempted). The placement-vocabulary lot then LANDED and drained both: `OverlayPlacement`'s inline sides are `inline-start`/`inline-end`, the `position-area` lowering emits the `self-*` logical family (`self-inline-start span-self-block-end`), `offsetMargins` is `marginInlineStart`/`marginInlineEnd`/`marginBlockStart`/`marginBlockEnd`, the measured branch resolves the side through the direction authority, and the slider's vertical tooltip anchors with `insetInlineStart` against `[data-placement='inline-start'|'inline-end']` skin transforms that mirror under `:dir(rtl)`. The two pins are REMOVED (slider 1 -> 0, overlay positioning 2 -> 0), pinned by `primitives/runtime/overlay/positioning/tests/OverlayPositioning.test.tsx`, `primitives/inputs/slider/tests/Slider.mark-label-direction.test.tsx` and the real-Chromium geometry suite `primitives/runtime/overlay/positioning/tests/OverlayPlacement.browser-geometry.integration.test.ts`. The PHYSICAL PLACEMENT VOCABULARY exception class therefore has no members and grants nothing: the retired physical spellings survive only as a documented input alias (`left` -> `inline-start`, `right` -> `inline-end`) which produces logical paint.

sites.reason: The inspector panel anchors to the POINTER (`left: state.position.x`). Pointer space is physical: the number is a viewport coordinate, and `insetInlineStart` would reinterpret it from the other edge under RTL and put the panel across the screen from the cursor. The file already carries this reason at the call site.

`left: adjusted.left` is the chart tooltip's own auto-flip result -- a viewport coordinate the component computed and clamped against the chart rect. Same class as the other measured-rect readers; it happens to live under charts, where the surrounding coordinate space is physical anyway.

MEASURED-SPACE class, parallel to the export-button entry. `projectGeometry` re-projects `placeholderRect.left`, a `getBoundingClientRect()` edge that `measure()` writes back as a fixed-position coordinate. The rect is already in physical coordinates, so a logical inset would mirror an already-mirrored measured edge and place the affixed element off its placeholder under RTL.

The zero-size pointer anchor the overlay positions against (`left: point.x`), placed at the contextmenu event's viewport coordinates. Same class as token-inspector: a measured pointer position, not a declared edge.

`left: dropdownPos.left` is a measured `getBoundingClientRect()` edge clamped to the viewport, the saved-views-menu precedent. The rect is already in physical coordinates; re-reading it as a logical inset would mirror an already-mirrored number.
`textarea.style.left = '-9999px'` parks the legacy clipboard-copy textarea offscreen. Not paint: -9999px is offscreen in both reading directions, and the element is removed on the next tick.
`left: position?.left` is the same measured-rect clamp as export-button: the value comes from a viewport measurement, so it is physical by construction.

patterns/foundation/engine-styles/modern.reason: `menuItemStyle`'s `textAlign: 'left'`. DEAD EXPORT: measured 0 consumers across all of src, alongside popupPanelStyle (0), menuListStyle (0) and pillBadgeStyle (0); only panelCardStyle (10) and pillBadgeSmStyle (5) are live. It retires under WO-RET-04 with the other three rather than being made logical, and this pin drops to zero when that retirement lands.

primitives/feedback/toast/compound/undo-.reason: The countdown bar track is pinned on BOTH inline edges (`left: 0` with `right: 0`) inside the toast surface, so it spans the full width and the reading direction moves neither edge. Clearing it to `inset-inline: 0` is a zero-pixel change.

primitives/runtime/overlay/backdrop/inde.reason: The fixed backdrop pins all four edges (`top/left/right/bottom: 0`) so it covers the viewport; both inline edges are fixed, so the reading direction moves nothing. Clearing it to `inset: 0` is a zero-pixel change.

primitives/feedback/progress/compound/ci.reason: `left: '50%'` centres the percentage label over the progress ring, paired with a translate that pulls it back by half its own width. A centred offset is symmetric, so the reading direction moves nothing; `insetInlineStart: '50%'` would be the idiom and a zero-pixel change.
